The definition of validation for ML models, as described in arXiv 2302.07103, focuses on the use of a sample of data to provide an unbiased evaluation of a model fit on the training dataset, particularly when tuning model hyperparameters. The goal is to achieve generalizable performance of the model.

In contrast, the validation for medical devices involves confirmation through objective evidence that the device fulfills its intended purpose and meets specified goals, which includes safety, performance, and clinical benefit. This validation is often referred to as narrow validation, as it specifically assesses whether the device meets its intended use.

The role of clinical evaluation in this context is crucial, as it involves assessing the clinical performance and safety of the medical device, ensuring that it achieves the specified goals in real-world settings. Clinical evaluations are part of the broader validation process for medical devices, which encompasses usability testing and other assessments to confirm that the device is fit for its intended purpose.
